source.name: NMRA S-9.2.2, Configuration Variables (approved standard, multifunction decoders)

notes: This is an NMRA baseline for MULTIFUNCTION (locomotive) decoders; accessory decoders have different CV assignments.
An NMRA CV assignment does not imply every decoder implements the CV or uses identical values. DecoderPro identifies the decoder model before applying manufacturer-specific definitions.
JMRI DecoderPro reference: https://github.com/JMRI/JMRI/tree/master/xml/decoders ; for CV28 compare lenz/railcom_cv28_29.xml, piko/cv28.xml and zimo profiles.
Reserved CVs or bits must not be interpreted as universally safe to change; actual decoder manuals and firmware revisions take precedence.
CV8 identifies the manufacturer when successfully read; writing CV8 may trigger a manufacturer-specific reset and should never be treated as an ordinary ID write.
Read-only descriptions do not modify the decoder and do not confirm support of an optional CV.

1.name: Primary (short) address
1.description: Short locomotive address 1–127; selected when CV29 bit 5 = 0. Value 3 is the standard uninstalled-decoder default.

2.name: Vstart
2.description: Motor drive level at first speed step; decoder motor control implementation may differ.

3.name: Acceleration rate
3.description: Acceleration momentum; zero disables this programmed acceleration delay.

4.name: Deceleration rate
4.description: Deceleration momentum; zero disables this programmed braking delay.

5.name: Vhigh (maximum drive)
5.description: Motor drive level at the highest speed step. Values 0 and 1 mean Vhigh is not used in the NMRA three-point curve.

6.name: Vmid (middle drive)
6.description: Motor drive level around the midpoint of the speed curve. Values 0 and 1 mean Vmid is not used in the NMRA three-point curve.

7.name: Manufacturer version
7.description: Manufacturer-defined decoder version/revision. The meaning of any write depends on the decoder manual.

8.name: Manufacturer ID
8.description: NMRA-assigned manufacturer identifier; this value is read-only under the NMRA specification.
8.warning: Do not write CV8 without the decoder manual: many manufacturers use writes to CV8 for reset or other special commands.

9.name: Total PWM period
9.description: Motor output PWM period/frequency configuration; optional and dependent on decoder motor control.

10.name: EMF feedback cutout
10.description: Speed-step threshold above which back-EMF motor control is cut out, where supported.

11.name: Packet timeout
11.description: Maximum period the decoder maintains speed without receiving a valid packet; see NMRA fail-safe requirements.

12.name: Power source conversion
12.description: Selects the alternate power source/mode when supported and permitted by CV29 bit 2.

13.name: Alternate-mode functions F1–F8
13.description: F1–F8 states when running in an alternate power mode without function packets.

14.name: Alternate-mode lights/F9–F12
14.description: Lighting and F9–F12 states in alternate power mode; bits 6–7 reserved.

15.name: Decoder lock select
15.description: Decoder lock selection value. A protected decoder accepts configuration writes when CV15 equals CV16; check the manual before changing.

16.name: Decoder lock ID
16.description: Decoder lock identity; CV16 = 0 disables locking under the standard.

17.name: Extended address (high byte)
17.description: High part of the two-byte locomotive address; used together with CV18 when CV29 bit 5 is enabled.

18.name: Extended address (low byte)
18.description: Low part of the two-byte locomotive address; used together with CV17 when CV29 bit 5 is enabled.

19.name: Consist address
19.description: Bits 0–6: consist address (0 means inactive); bit 7: relative reversed direction.

21.name: Consist functions F1-F8
21.description: Bits 0-7 select whether F1-F8 also respond to the consist address.

22.name: Consist functions FL/F9-F12
22.description: Selects whether lighting and F9-F12 also respond to the consist address.

23.name: Acceleration adjustment
23.description: Signed acceleration adjustment relative to CV3, typically for consist operation; bit 7 is the subtract flag.

24.name: Deceleration adjustment
24.description: Signed deceleration adjustment relative to CV4, typically for consist operation; bit 7 is the subtract flag.

25.name: Speed table / mid-cab step selection
25.description: Selects a factory speed table or midpoint speed-step position on supporting decoders. Values 0 and 1 mean it is not used.

27.name: Automatic stopping configuration
27.description: Selects automatic braking/stopping triggers, where supported. Do not confuse with CV28 RailCom.

bits.name: Asymmetric DCC, right rail more positive
Asymmetric DCC, left rail more positive

28.name: Bi-directional communication (RailCom) configuration
28.description: The approved NMRA S-9.2.2 baseline controls decoder-initiated transmissions when CV29 bit 3 is set. JMRI/decoder manufacturers can define different meanings for CV28 bits, including Channel 1/2 and RailComPlus; these must be selected by decoder model.
28.warning: Decoder-specific! JMRI Lenz/PIKO profiles map bits 0/1 to RailCom channels; PIKO SmartDecoder XP5.1 uses bit 3 for an address-broadcast option, and some PIKO profiles use bit 7 for RailComPlus. These meanings are not universal NMRA assignments. Preserve reserved/unknown bits and check the precise decoder model.

bits.name: Broadcast initiated by Signal Controlled Influence

29.name: Decoder configuration
29.description: Multifunction-decoder configuration flags. The bit meanings below are from the approved NMRA S-9.2.2 standard.

bits.name: Headlight (FL/F0) command location
bits.on: FL in function group instruction (28/128-step style)

30.name: Decoder error information
30.description: Manufacturer-specific error code; zero indicates no error under the NMRA standard.

31.name: Index high byte
31.description: High byte of the index page used to access indexed CV257–512; interpretation depends on the decoder.

32.name: Index low byte
32.description: Low byte of the index page used to access indexed CV257–512; interpretation depends on the decoder.

65.name: Kick start
65.description: Extra motor drive supplied when transitioning from stop to the first speed step.

66.name: Forward trim
66.description: Forward motor-drive scaling factor n/128 under the NMRA specification; 0 means trim is not implemented.

95.name: Reverse trim
95.description: Reverse motor-drive scaling factor n/128 under the NMRA specification; 0 means trim is not implemented.

105.name: User identifier 1
105.description: User-defined identification value; not a guaranteed unique hardware ID.

106.description: User-defined identification value; not a guaranteed unique hardware ID.

892.description: Dynamic value representing decoder load (manufacturer/decoder support required).

20-20.name: NMRA reserved CV
20-20.description: Reserved in the approved S-9.2.2 multifunction-decoder mapping; do not infer a standard function.

26-26.name: NMRA reserved CV
26-26.description: Reserved in the approved S-9.2.2 multifunction-decoder mapping; do not infer a standard function.

47-64.name: Manufacturer-specific CV range
47-64.description: Reserved for manufacturer use; no universal bit or value meanings. Select the exact DecoderPro decoder definition or manufacturer manual.

67-94.name: Extended speed table
67-94.description: 28 individual motor-drive curve values (CV67 to CV94), selected when CV29 bit 4 is on.

96-104.name: NMRA reserved CV range
96-104.description: Reserved by the NMRA in the approved multifunction-decoder specification; do not assume a universal function.

107-111.name: NMRA reserved / extended ID area
107-111.description: Reserved in the approved 2012 standard. Some newer draft specifications and decoder implementations use parts of this area for extended manufacturer/version identifiers; verify the exact decoder.

112-256.name: Manufacturer-specific CV range
112-256.description: Reserved for manufacturer use; no standard cross-manufacturer meaning. See the specific JMRI decoder profile.

257-512.name: Indexed CV area
257-512.description: Indexed CV pages, normally selected using CV31 and CV32. A numeric CV alone may not identify the parameter without the active page.

513-879.name: NMRA reserved CV range
513-879.description: Reserved for future NMRA use in the approved 2012 multifunction decoder map; later drafts or manufacturer implementations may differ.

880-891.name: Dynamic CV area
880-891.description: NMRA dynamic/volatile CV area; not a generic persistent user configuration field.

896-1024.name: SUSI sound/function module CV area
896-1024.description: Configuration space for SUSI sound and function modules; definitions vary by module/manufacturer.
